# [P2] Standalone SVG renders solid black in Inkscape after colors become CSS variables

PR #152 replaces literal SVG colors with `var(--pm-...)` values without literal paint fallbacks. Inkscape 1.4 does not resolve those custom properties, so both the background and foreground become black and the chart is unreadable. The same synthetic input renders legibly before this change.

Affected head: `130c2f0b06a28dabe08aa058c7ea75d1d585ccc1` ([index.ts:2114–2121](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/130c2f0b06a28dabe08aa058c7ea75d1d585ccc1/index.ts#L2114-L2121), with the same paint pattern throughout `renderSvg`). Base: `cc4e5d4d1c0e390722f982ee80833d7e54deec4b`.

## Self-contained reproduction

Prerequisites: a checkout at the affected head with its normal dependencies installed, supported Node, Inkscape 1.4, and Python 3 with Pillow for the optional pixel oracle. Run from the repository root after the normal build:

```sh
npm run build
REPRO_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$REPRO_HOME" TZ=UTC DO_NOT_TRACK=1 PM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 PM_SENTRY_DISABLED=1 node --input-type=module <<'JS'
import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { renderSvg } from './dist/index.js';

const start = new Date('2026-10-12T00:00:00Z');
const opts = {
  weeks: 1, width: 320, groupBy: 'type', statusFilter: 'all',
  today: start, criticalPath: false, criticalOnly: false,
  schedule: false, defaultDuration: 5, progress: true, milestones: [],
};
const rows = ['open', 'in_progress', 'blocked', 'closed', 'canceled'].map((status, i) => ({
  item: {
    id: `item-${i}`, title: `Review ${status}`, status,
    type: 'Task', priority: 1, deadline: '2026-10-16',
  },
  group: 'Task', startWeek: 0, endWeek: 0,
  start, end: new Date('2026-10-16T00:00:00Z'),
  critical: false, overdue: i === 0, progress: 50,
  slackDays: null, infeasible: false,
}));
writeFileSync('gantt-repro.svg', renderSvg(rows, opts, start));
JS
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$REPRO_HOME" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$REPRO_HOME/.cache" \
  inkscape gantt-repro.svg --export-type=png --export-filename=gantt-repro.png
python3 - <<'PY'
from collections import Counter
from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('gantt-repro.png').convert('RGB')
colors = Counter(im.getdata())
print('size:', im.size, 'unique RGB colors:', len(colors))
print('most common:', colors.most_common(3))
assert len(colors) > 1, 'The whole chart rasterized to a single color'
PY
```

`renderSvg` is an actual named export in both the current source and `dist/index.d.ts`. This fixture is fully synthetic; no tracker initialization or SDK reads are required by the renderer.

Actual with Inkscape `1.4 (e7c3feb100, 2024-10-09)`:

```text
size: (576, 480) unique RGB colors: 1
most common: [((0, 0, 0), 276480)]
```

The output PNG is entirely black. Inkscape returns success, with unsupported-CSS parsing warnings. Running the same reproduction on the base commit yields a legible 422×312 PNG with 632 RGB colors. Both images were visually inspected as well as pixel-counted.

## Expected and acceptance

Standalone SVG exports should remain readable when imported or converted in an ordinary desktop SVG consumer. Keep literal presentation-attribute colors for consumers without CSS-variable support, with optional CSS overrides for capable browser renderers. Adding a fallback argument inside `var()` alone will not help a consumer that does not implement `var()`.

Add a non-browser rendering check: the five-status fixture must retain a visible paper background, text, status fills and outlines in Inkscape 1.4, while existing light/dark browser checks continue to pass.

## Verification scope

The exact base/head pure renderer implementations were exercised against Inkscape on synthetic rows, with isolated HOME, TZ=UTC and tracking disabled. The public named export and argument shape above were verified in current source/declarations; the full package build/SDK-backed import was not executed during this focused review. No live tracker, Core command, paid API or broad test suite was used. Chrome-only coverage cannot detect this consumer regression.

> **@unbraind** (2026-10-18T13:03:36Z)
>
> ### Native Inkscape 1.4 follow-up: all-black chart fixed, canceled labels still disappear
> 
> Reproduced on current main `37452470fbc44c5977d2906cdd395cb9a85b530d` (package `2026.10.18`, merged #152), using Inkscape `1.4 (e7c3feb100, 2024-10-09)`.
> 
> The original whole-chart-black regression is fixed. The same five-status synthetic fixture from this issue now renders a 648×480 image with 1,108 RGB colors, visible paper, item text and the other status fills. The original affected renderer at `130c2f0b06a28dabe08aa058c7ea75d1d585ccc1` still produces the expected negative control: 576×480, exactly one RGB color, black.
> 
> **Remaining reproduced defect:** the canceled row's status chip and the canceled legend chip become solid carbon, hiding their labels; its timeline bar also becomes carbon. Inkscape exits successfully.
> 
> The canceled background token is [`transparent`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/37452470fbc44c5977d2906cdd395cb9a85b530d/brand-values.ts#L15-L17). The [SVG paint serialization](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/37452470fbc44c5977d2906cdd395cb9a85b530d/index.ts#L2206-L2218) emits it unchanged as `fill="transparent"`. On this native renderer, that paint falls back to the inherited root carbon. This is materially narrower than the old whole-chart failure, but still fails this issue's five-status native acceptance and the [Triplicate task's explicit-status requirement](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/37452470fbc44c5977d2906cdd395cb9a85b530d/.agents/pm/tasks/pm-gantt-chart-triplicate.toon).
> 
> **Measured on the original fixture**
> - Canceled row label crop `(435,344,526,358)`: 1,272 of 1,274 pixels are carbon; comparing against the same SVG with text removed finds zero glyph pixels with a channel difference greater than 16
> - Canceled legend label crop `(521,395,627,411)`: 1,694 of 1,696 pixels are carbon; the same glyph oracle also finds zero
> - A diagnostic change only to the generated SVG, replacing `fill="transparent"` with `fill="none"`, restores 145 and 144 visible glyph pixels respectively (176 each when counting every nonzero difference). No renderer implementation was changed
> - Source and committed-dist pure renderer outputs, and their native PNGs, are byte-identical for this fixture
> 
> **Small standalone reproduction of the paint failure** (no dependencies, SDK or tracker needed):
> ```sh
> cat > transparent.svg <<'SVG'
> <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="160" height="40" fill="#1B2340"><rect width="160" height="40" fill="#F3F5F8"/><rect x="5" y="5" width="150" height="30" fill="transparent"/><text x="15" y="25" fill="#1B2340">canceled</text></svg>
> SVG
> sed 's/fill="transparent"/fill="none"/' transparent.svg > none.svg
> REPRO_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
> for name in transparent none; do
>   env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$REPRO_HOME" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$REPRO_HOME/.cache" TZ=UTC \
>     inkscape "$name.svg" --export-type=png --export-filename="$name.png"
> done
> ```
> Actual: `transparent.png` has an unreadable solid-carbon rectangle; the `none.png` control has a readable canceled label over paper. In the rectangle crop `(5,5,155,35)`, the first has 4,496/4,500 exact-carbon pixels; the control has 137 colors and 4,238 paper pixels. Both outputs were visually inspected.
> 
> **Expected / acceptance:** all five states, including canceled row and legend labels, must be readable in an ordinary Inkscape 1.4 import/conversion. Serialize transparent/alpha paints in a native-compatible form, retain the intended canceled outline/state distinction, and add a per-state native glyph/background check. Keep the whole-chart negative control, source/dist parity, and existing browser light/dark checks. The output-only `none` experiment establishes the immediate cause; it is not a complete implementation or outline-compatibility proof.
> 
> **Scope:** tests used exact pure renderer/helper implementations extracted unchanged from the immutable source and dist, synthetic rows, isolated HOME and UTC. No live tracker, SDK-backed package import, dependency installation, full local build or browser rerun was performed. The merged-head [CI run](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/actions/runs/39124820519) independently passes Node 22.18 and Node 26; its Node 26 npm/Bun gates each report 254/254 tests and 100% runtime line/branch/function coverage. That does not cover this native canceled-state failure.
> 
> Checked all-status issues/PRs, this issue's three existing replies, all 27 resolved PR review threads, and the 107 canonical PM records before adding this evidence here. The existing portability item remains the appropriate place to track it; no duplicate issue is needed.
